the stereotype threat literature is a literature of the mind, and that the mind is a literature of stereotype threat.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

stereotype threat is an instance of a general phenomenon in which a task is performed less efficiently when the cognitive resources that the task requires are concurrently used to perform a secondary task.
stereotype threat has a profound impact on cognitive processing, which is both detrimental and malleable.

stereotype threat has a negative effect on performance, especially on tasks that are highly dependent on working memory resources, but that this effect is attenuated when the task is practiced to the extent that it is retrieved from long-term memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive resources that are used to process a stereotype are the same ones that are used to perform a task, and this is true whether the task is math or memory.
the effects of stereotype threat are mediated by working memory resources and that this can be exploited for both alleviation and spillover effects.
the effects of stereotype threat are not mysterious, and they can be mitigated by capitalizing on our understanding of the mechanisms of stereotype threat.
